SHEET 01

Profile

I'm an Engineering Technology student finishing a Design minor at Sam Houston State University, focused on parametric CAD, assembly design, and turning models into physical, printed parts. My coursework runs from industrial design and drafting through advanced CAD modeling, product development, and virtual and augmented reality — and I like projects that carry a design all the way from sketch to a working prototype.

Alongside coursework I work as a CAD operator for SHSU's Facilities Planning & Construction office, updating drawings against real field measurements, and I teach AutoCAD, SolidWorks, and Creo as a TA — so I spend as much time explaining models as building them.

SHEET 03

Multi-Part Boat Structure

A team project to model and manufacture a multi-part boat as individual CAD components, then bring them together into one coordinated assembly. Each teammate modeled a subset of parts — hull, cabin walls, funnel, windows, ladder, lamp, stern — while the group tracked fit, tolerances, and version control through a shared file structure.

The build included full engineering drawings with dimensions, an exploded-view assembly diagram, and 3D-printed components on a Prusa Core One after several rounds of correcting slicer and support settings.

ROLETeam of three — CAD modeling, drawings & assembly
TOOLSCreo Parametric, Prusa Core One (FDM)
Assembly designTechnical drawings3D printing
SHEET 04

Interactive Specimen Exhibit

A twelve-panel, dodecahedron-shaped display built to let visitors identify specimens up close through clear viewing windows set into each face, paired with printed ID panels — used here for an exotic fruit fly and coconut rhinoceros beetle exhibit. I worked on the physical build: cutting and assembling the pentagonal wood frames, sheathing the enclosure in plywood, and finishing it for outdoor use.

It runs alongside a separate research project I co-authored on augmented reality for clinical training — an AR application aimed at improving accuracy in clinical foot-palpation practice, published at STE 2026 — which explores the same idea of letting someone examine a subject up close without the constraints of the physical object itself.

ROLEFabrication — framing, assembly, finishing
MATERIALSPine framing, plywood, acrylic panels
FabricationExhibit designAR research
SHEET 05

Process Skid — Master Model

A class project modeling a modular process skid as a single master assembly: structural steel framing, an elevated platform with railing and ladder access, a vertical vessel, and the piping routed between them. Built to practice managing a large multi-component assembly where every part has to reference back to one coordinated structure.

ROLEIndividual coursework — full assembly
SCOPEStructural frame, vessel, piping, platform
Assembly modelingStructural design

Fabrication & Prototyping

A rotating set of smaller CAD-to-print exercises — practicing multi-part assemblies, internal structure, and print-friendly geometry on the Prusa Core One outside of larger team projects.

Rapid prototypingAdditive manufacturing
SHEET 07

Facilities Fire Evacuation Plans

As a CAD operator for SHSU's Facilities Planning & Construction office, I maintain the university's official fire evacuation plans and building floor plans in AutoCAD — coordinating exit routes, fire extinguisher and alarm panel locations, and ADA access points against the standard campus legend, then producing the posted, code-compliant sheets for facilities like the Smith Hutson Building and Bowers Stadium.

Much of the work starts in the field: walking a space with a printed set, red-lining elevations and dimensions against what's actually built, then bringing those corrections back into the model so the drawings stay accurate as buildings change.

ROLECAD operator — Facilities Planning & Construction
TOOLSAutoCAD, field verification & red-lining
Life-safety drawingsAs-built documentationFacilities CAD
